answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a scarce, withdrawable stake before it may issue work requests. Peers challenge suspicious clusters by asking them to complete a small, unpredictable task, then slash the stake for failures or duplicate credentials proven through shared control. The ember of a whisper network can flag candidates, but evidence and penalties govern enforcement. Creating many identities therefore ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making a harbor of fake accounts costly rather than free.
